sentences.text:
Gobinda @ Rabindra Nath Roy@ Bhuttu vs The State Of West
Bengal on 27 February, 2026

1
 Item No.1 Court No.7 
 S U P R E M E C O U R T O F I N D

Record Of Proceedings
 Criminal Appeal No.871/2026
 Gobinda @ Rabindra Nath Roy@ Bhuttu

Versus
 The State Of West Bengal & Anr.
[Only Prayer For Bail Is Listed Under This Item]
This matter was called on for hearing today.

Coram :
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice J.B. Pardiwala
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice K.V. Viswanathan

For Appellant(s) :
 Ms. Anwesha Saha, Aor
 Mr. Salim Ansari, Adv.
 Mr. Nitish Shani, Adv.
 For Respondent(s) :
UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.

The appellant was put to trial in Sessions Trial No.04(02)/2018 arising out of Sessions Case No.
82 of 2017 for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 417 respectively of the Indian Penal Code (for short, IPC).
2.

The Trial Court held the appellant guilty of the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo seven years of rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment, to suffer further simple imprisonment for a period of one year.
He was sentenced to undergo six months of rigorous imprisonment for the offence punishable under Section 417 IPC.
3. The Criminal Appeal preferred by the appellant in the High Court also failed.

sentences.text: 4. In such circumstances, the appellant is here before us with the present application seeking bail pending the final disposal of his Criminal Appeal.
5. We have already granted leave in the matter.
6. We heard Ms. Anwesha Saha, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/convict.
7. As per the Office Report dated 26-2-2026, notice of lodgement of petition of appeal was issued but no certificate of service has been received from the High Court so far.
8. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of this case and also considering the nature of the evidence on record, we are persuaded to pass an order of interim bail.

9. We could have passed an order today itself ordering release of the appellant on bail, however,
since the State is not before us, we would like to hear the respondent-State and thereafter pass further orders.
10. We order that the appellant shall be released on interim bail, subject to terms and conditions that the Trial Court may deem fit to impose.

11. Post the matter for further hearing on 10-4-2026.
 (VISHAL ANAND) (POOJA SHARMA)
ASTT.
REGISTRAR-cum-PS COURT MASTER (NSH)
